bookends.command: Quiz me on porting a Godot game to Unity and Unreal, with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms GameObject, Actor, Prefab, override, ScriptableObject, Event Dispatcher, FixedUpdate, Layer Collision Matrix, Object Type and Z-up. For each case I must name the exact term in the right engine and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply.

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. People moving from Godot to Unity often say a node is a component. Not quite. A Godot node is one object, like a Unity GameObject. Where Unity adds components, Godot uses a node type and child nodes. The Unity and Unreal names come from their documentation, not from runs. This film goes through the terms, each one shown with all three names.

beats.narration_text: A table with a column for each engine, filling one row at a time. The first row is Scene, Level, Map. A Godot scene, a Unity Scene and an Unreal Level are each a saved, reusable tree of objects, and Unreal calls its level file a Map. A level is narrower, one playable space. For example, in Godot the first level of a platformer is a scene file, and so is the coin placed in it, but only the first is a level.
